fsms.stateDoc:
States of the gait DFA: the seven gait phases of the reference leg, in
stride order, plus the sink state `invalid`. The percentages are typical
boundaries in percent of the stride (Perry); the pipeline measures the actual
ones per trial (`HasPhaseAttrs`).
fsms.eventDoc:
Input symbols of the gait DFA: the gait events that bound the phases, named
from the reference leg.

states.name: loadingResponse
states.doc:
Stance, about 0–10 %: the leg takes the body's weight. From initial contact
to opposite toe-off.

states.name: midStance
states.doc:
Stance, about 10–30 %: the body passes over the supporting foot. From
opposite toe-off to heel-off.

states.name: terminalStance
states.doc:
Stance, about 30–50 %: the heel rises and the body moves ahead of the foot.
From heel-off to opposite initial contact.

states.name: preSwing
states.doc:
Stance, about 50–60 %: both feet are on the ground and the weight shifts to
the opposite leg. From opposite initial contact to toe-off.

states.name: initialSwing
states.doc:
Swing, about 60–73 %: the foot lifts and the thigh moves forward. From
toe-off to feet adjacent.

states.name: midSwing
states.doc:
Swing, about 73–87 %: the swinging leg passes the supporting leg. From feet
adjacent to tibia vertical.

states.name: terminalSwing
states.doc:
Swing, about 87–100 %: the leg reaches forward for the next contact. From
tibia vertical to initial contact.

states.name: invalid
states.doc:
Sink state: an event out of order leads here, and every event keeps the
automaton here.

events.name: initialContact
events.doc:
The reference foot touches the ground (an instant, decision D-001). Ends
terminal swing and opens loading response.

events.name: oppositeToeOff
events.doc: The opposite foot leaves the ground. Ends loading response.

events.name: heelOff
events.doc: The reference heel rises from the ground. Ends mid-stance.

events.name: oppositeInitialContact
events.doc: The opposite foot touches the ground. Ends terminal stance.

events.name: toeOff
events.doc: The reference foot leaves the ground. Ends pre-swing.

events.name: feetAdjacent
events.doc: The swinging foot passes the supporting foot. Ends initial swing.

events.name: tibiaVertical
events.doc: The tibia of the swinging leg reaches vertical. Ends mid-swing.

stateLists.name: GaitPhase.phases
stateLists.doc:
The seven gait phases in stride order, from loading response to terminal
swing: the phase bands of the timeline.

stateLists.name: GaitPhase.stance
stateLists.doc: The stance phases in stride order: from initial contact to toe-off.

stateLists.name: GaitPhase.swing
stateLists.doc: The swing phases in stride order: from toe-off to the next initial contact.

words.name: strideWord
words.doc:
One stride from the start state: the seven events in order, from opposite
toe-off to the next initial contact.

fsms.eventDoc: User input events of the movement player.

states.name: idle
states.doc: The playhead rests at the start of the cycle and the inspector is closed.

states.name: playing
states.doc: The animation runs and the playhead advances.

states.name: paused
states.doc: The animation holds still at the playhead's frame.

states.name: scrubbing
states.doc: The user drags the playhead; the frame on screen follows the pointer.

states.name: inspectingNode
states.doc:
The inspector is open on a selected node; the animation holds still at
the playhead's frame.

events.name: stop
events.doc: The user presses stop: the playhead returns to the start.

events.name: selectNode
events.doc: The user clicks a node, in the 3D view or the graph view.

events.name: reachEnd
events.doc: The playhead reaches the end of the recording (sent by the player).

words.name: resetWord
words.doc: Release the playhead, then stop: the reset word of the player.

stages.name: buildModel
stages.doc:
Merge the trunk, arm, and neck muscles of the upper-body models onto the
scaled Rajagopal model, give the head its own body behind a neck joint, and
add the neck angles that hold the head level in space to the joint angles
(D-008, D-009, D-010).

stages.name: loadModel
stages.doc: Load the merged model and the walking trial with the OpenSim API.

stages.name: runStaticOpt
stages.doc: Static optimisation: muscle activations per frame.

stages.name: computeMomentArms
stages.doc:
Moment arm and muscle-tendon length per muscle, coordinate, and frame;
length velocity gives concentric or eccentric work.

stages.name: segmentPhases
stages.doc:
Detect gait events and drive the generated gait FSM to label each frame
with its phase.

stages.name: labelRoles
stages.doc:
Classify each muscle per phase and joint action as main mover, helper,
stabiliser, or antagonist.

stages.name: enrichAnatomy
stages.doc: Add common names, ontology identifiers, attachments, and innervation.

stages.name: exportMeshes
stages.doc:
Convert the model's bone geometry to glTF, each mesh multiplied by its
scale factors from the merged model.

stages.name: exportMusclePaths
stages.doc:
Write muscle path points per frame for the tube renderer, with the
bounds of the stride the knowledge graph describes.

stages.name: exportDynamics
stages.doc:
Write each muscle's moment about each joint coordinate, and the
coordinate's angle, per frame, for the dynamics panel.

artefacts.name: scaledModel

The Rajagopal full-body model scaled to the walking subject: the base

artefacts.name: uberon

artefacts.name: mergeRecipe
artefacts.doc:
The merge recipe: the source models, the Rajagopal body each source body

artefacts.name: mergedModel
artefacts.doc:
The scaled Rajagopal model with the trunk, arm, and neck muscles merged

`ikMotion`'s joint coordinates plus, per frame, the neck angles that

Bodies (with their mesh files), joints, coordinates, and muscles (with

artefacts.name: grf

artefacts.name: activations

theorems.name: BioMech.Kind.regional_iff
theorems.statement: ∀ (k : Kind), k.regional = true ↔ k ≠ Kind.movement ∧ k ≠ Kind.phase

Every anatomy kind and the joint action carry a region; movements and
phases are the two kinds without one.

theorems.name: BioMech.Gait.GaitPhase.mem_phases
theorems.statement: ∀ (p : GaitPhase), p ∈ GaitPhase.phases ↔ p ≠ GaitPhase.invalid
theorems.doc: `GaitPhase.phases` holds exactly the states other than `invalid`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Gait.GaitEvent.mem_all

theorems.name: BioMech.Gait.step_of_mem
theorems.statement: ∀ t ∈ transitions, gaitDfa.step t.1 t.2.1 = t.2.2
theorems.doc: Every row of `transitions` is a step of the gait DFA.

theorems.name: BioMech.Gait.step_eq_invalid_of_not_mem
theorems.statement:
∀ (s : GaitPhase) (e : GaitEvent),
  (s, e) ∉ List.map (fun t => (t.1, t.2.1)) transitions → gaitDfa.step s e = GaitPhase.invalid
theorems.doc: Every (phase, event) pair absent from `transitions` goes to `invalid`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Gait.transitions_keys_nodup
theorems.statement: (List.map (fun t => (t.1, t.2.1)) transitions).Nodup
theorems.doc:
Each (phase, event) pair heads at most one row, so the table is a function
and emitters may key it by `(from, event)`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Gait.transitions_phases
theorems.statement: ∀ t ∈ transitions, t.1 ∈ GaitPhase.phases ∧ t.2.2 ∈ GaitPhase.phases
theorems.doc:
Every row starts and ends in one of the seven phases; `invalid` appears only
as the default target.

theorems.name: BioMech.Gait.one_event_per_phase
theorems.statement: ∀ s ∈ GaitPhase.phases, (List.filter (fun x => x.1 == s) transitions).length = 1
theorems.doc:
Each of the seven phases ends at exactly one event: the gait cycle is a
single loop through the phases.

theorems.name: BioMech.Gait.event_opens_phase
theorems.statement: ∀ ep ∈ GaitEvent.all.zip GaitPhase.phases, ∃ s, (s, ep.1, ep.2) ∈ transitions
theorems.doc:
`GaitEvent.all` and `GaitPhase.phases` run side by side: the event at each
position opens the phase at the same position.

theorems.name: BioMech.Gait.phases_eq_stance_append_swing
theorems.statement: GaitPhase.phases = GaitPhase.stance ++ GaitPhase.swing
theorems.doc: The stance phases, then the swing phases, are the seven phases in stride order.

theorems.name: BioMech.Gait.period_changes
theorems.statement:
∀ t ∈ transitions,
  (t.1 ∈ GaitPhase.stance ∧ t.2.2 ∈ GaitPhase.swing ↔ t.2.1 = GaitEvent.toeOff) ∧
    (t.1 ∈ GaitPhase.swing ∧ t.2.2 ∈ GaitPhase.stance ↔ t.2.1 = GaitEvent.initialContact)
theorems.doc:
A row leads from stance to swing exactly at toe-off, and from swing to
stance exactly at initial contact.

theorems.name: BioMech.Gait.strideWord_returns
theorems.statement: gaitDfa.eval strideWord = gaitDfa.start
theorems.doc: One stride takes the start state back to the start state.

theorems.name: BioMech.Gait.strideWord_accepted
theorems.statement: strideWord ∈ gaitDfa.accepts
theorems.doc: One stride is accepted.

theorems.name: BioMech.Gait.strides_accepted
theorems.statement: ∀ w ∈ KStar.kstar {strideWord}, w ∈ gaitDfa.accepts
theorems.doc:
Every whole number of strides (the Kleene star of `strideWord`, zero strides
included) is accepted.

theorems.name: BioMech.Gait.stride_trace
theorems.statement:
List.map (fun n => gaitDfa.eval (List.take n strideWord)) (List.range strideWord.length) =
  GaitPhase.phases
theorems.doc:
The states along `strideWord`, after each of its first seven prefixes, are
the seven phases in stride order.

theorems.name: BioMech.Gait.every_phase_visited
theorems.statement: ∀ p ∈ GaitPhase.phases, ∃ n < strideWord.length, gaitDfa.eval (List.take n strideWord) = p
theorems.doc: Every one of the seven phases is the state after some prefix of `strideWord`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Gait.step_invalid
theorems.statement: ∀ (e : GaitEvent), gaitDfa.step GaitPhase.invalid e = GaitPhase.invalid
theorems.doc: Every event keeps `invalid` in `invalid`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Gait.evalFrom_invalid
theorems.statement: ∀ (w : List GaitEvent), gaitDfa.evalFrom GaitPhase.invalid w = GaitPhase.invalid
theorems.doc: `invalid` is absorbing: every word keeps the automaton in `invalid`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Gait.rejects_of_eval_invalid
theorems.statement:
∀ {u : List GaitEvent},
  gaitDfa.eval u = GaitPhase.invalid → ∀ (v : List GaitEvent), u ++ v ∉ gaitDfa.accepts
theorems.doc: Once a prefix lands in `invalid`, every extension of it is rejected.

theorems.name: BioMech.Gait.skipped_heelOff
theorems.statement: gaitDfa.eval [GaitEvent.oppositeToeOff, GaitEvent.oppositeInitialContact] = GaitPhase.invalid
theorems.doc:
Example: opposite initial contact right after opposite toe-off skips heel-off,
so the automaton lands in `invalid`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Gait.skipped_heelOff_rejected
theorems.statement:
∀ (v : List GaitEvent),
  [GaitEvent.oppositeToeOff, GaitEvent.oppositeInitialContact] ++ v ∉ gaitDfa.accepts
theorems.doc: Example: every word that starts by skipping heel-off is rejected.

theorems.name: BioMech.Ui.evalFrom_resetWord
theorems.statement: ∀ (s : UiState), uiDfa.evalFrom s resetWord = UiState.idle
theorems.doc: `resetWord` takes every state to `idle`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Ui.reaches_idle
theorems.statement: ∀ (s : UiState), ∃ w, uiDfa.evalFrom s w = UiState.idle

theorems.name: BioMech.Ui.step_scrubbing
theorems.statement:
∀ (e : UiEvent),
  uiDfa.step UiState.scrubbing e =
    if e = UiEvent.scrubEnd then UiState.paused else UiState.scrubbing
theorems.doc:
The step from `scrubbing`: `paused` on `scrubEnd`, `scrubbing` on every other
event.

theorems.name: BioMech.Ui.step_scrubbing_mem
theorems.statement:
∀ (e : UiEvent),
  uiDfa.step UiState.scrubbing e = UiState.scrubbing ∨
    uiDfa.step UiState.scrubbing e = UiState.paused
theorems.doc: Every event from `scrubbing` leads to `scrubbing` or `paused`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Ui.step_scrubbing_scrubEnd
theorems.statement: uiDfa.step UiState.scrubbing UiEvent.scrubEnd = UiState.paused
theorems.doc: `scrubEnd` leads from `scrubbing` to `paused`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Ui.evalFrom_scrubbing
theorems.statement: ∀ (w : List UiEvent), UiEvent.scrubEnd ∉ w → uiDfa.evalFrom UiState.scrubbing w = UiState.scrubbing
theorems.doc: A word free of `scrubEnd` keeps `scrubbing` in `scrubbing`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Ui.scrubbing_ends_in_paused
theorems.statement:
∀ (w v : List UiEvent),
  UiEvent.scrubEnd ∉ w →
    uiDfa.evalFrom UiState.scrubbing (w ++ UiEvent.scrubEnd :: v) = uiDfa.evalFrom UiState.paused v
theorems.doc:
Scrubbing ends in `paused`: from `scrubbing`, the first `scrubEnd` of a word
lands in `paused`, and the rest of the word runs from there.

theorems.name: BioMech.rank_lt_of_transGen
theorems.statement:
∀ {V : Type u} {G : Digraph V} (r : V → ℕ),
  (∀ (u v : V), G.Adj u v → r u < r v) → ∀ {u v : V}, Relation.TransGen G.Adj u v → r u < r v
theorems.doc: A rank that grows along every edge grows strictly along every path.

theorems.name: BioMech.acyclic_of_rank
theorems.statement: ∀ {V : Type u} {G : Digraph V} (r : V → ℕ), (∀ (u v : V), G.Adj u v → r u < r v) → Acyclic G
theorems.doc: A rank that grows strictly along every edge proves acyclicity.

theorems.name: BioMech.acyclic_ofEdges_of_rank
theorems.statement: ∀ {V : Type u} (es : List (V × V)) (r : V → ℕ), (∀ e ∈ es, r e.1 < r e.2) → Acyclic (ofEdges es)
theorems.doc: The rank lemma in list form: the check runs over the listed edges only.

theorems.name: BioMech.ReachesOnlyVia.reaches
theorems.statement: ∀ {V : Type u} {G : Digraph V} {u x v : V}, ReachesOnlyVia G u x v → Relation.TransGen G.Adj u v
theorems.doc: Some path leads from `u` to `v`.

theorems.name: BioMech.ReachesOnlyVia.cut
theorems.statement:
∀ {V : Type u} {G : Digraph V} {u x v : V},
  ReachesOnlyVia G u x v → ¬Relation.TransGen (deleteVertex G x).Adj u v
theorems.doc: Every path from `u` to `v` visits `x`.

theorems.name: BioMech.deleteVertex_ofEdges
theorems.statement:
∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] (es : List (V × V)) (x : V),
  deleteVertex (ofEdges es) x = ofEdges (List.filter (fun e => decide (e.1 ≠ x ∧ e.2 ≠ x)) es)
theorems.doc: Deleting a vertex from an edge-list digraph filters its edge list.

theorems.name: BioMech.Reach.mem_image

∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {es : List (V × V)} {S : List V} {w : V},

theorems.name: BioMech.Reach.subset_closeN
theorems.statement:
∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {es : List (V × V)} (n : ℕ) (S : List V),
  ∀ v ∈ S, v ∈ closeN es n S

theorems.name: BioMech.Reach.closeN_sound
theorems.statement:
∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {es : List (V × V)} (u : V) (n : ℕ) (S : List V),
  (∀ s ∈ S, Relation.TransGen (ofEdges es).Adj u s) →
    ∀ v ∈ closeN es n S, Relation.TransGen (ofEdges es).Adj u v
theorems.doc:
Every vertex the closure adds is reachable from `u`, given a start set
reachable from `u`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Reach.closed_union_image
theorems.statement:
∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {es : List (V × V)} {S : List V},
  Closed es S → Closed es (S ∪ image es S)

theorems.name: BioMech.Reach.closed_closeN_of_closed
theorems.statement:
∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {es : List (V × V)} (n : ℕ) {S : List V},
  Closed es S → Closed es (closeN es n S)

theorems.name: BioMech.Reach.missing_union_lt
theorems.statement:
∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {es : List (V × V)} {S : List V},
  ¬Closed es S → missing es (S ∪ image es S) < missing es S
theorems.doc: A round of closure on an open set adds an edge target that was missing.

theorems.name: BioMech.Reach.closed_closeN
theorems.statement:
∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {es : List (V × V)} (n : ℕ) (S : List V),
  missing es S ≤ n → Closed es (closeN es n S)

theorems.name: BioMech.closed_reachable
theorems.statement: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {es : List (V × V)} (u : V), Reach.Closed es (reachable es u)
theorems.doc: `es.length` rounds of closure reach a closed set.

theorems.name: BioMech.transGen_iff_mem_reachable
theorems.statement:
∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {es : List (V × V)} {u v : V},
  Relation.TransGen (ofEdges es).Adj u v ↔ v ∈ reachable es u
theorems.doc:
Reachability computed by closure agrees with the transitive closure of the
adjacency.

theorems.name: BioMech.IsTopoOrder.nodup
theorems.statement: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {G : Digraph V} {l : List V}, IsTopoOrder G l → l.Nodup
theorems.doc: Each vertex appears at most once.

theorems.name: BioMech.IsTopoOrder.complete
theorems.statement:
∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {G : Digraph V} {l : List V},
  IsTopoOrder G l → ∀ (v : V), v ∈ l
theorems.doc: Each vertex appears.

theorems.name: BioMech.IsTopoOrder.forward
theorems.statement:
∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {G : Digraph V} {l : List V},
  IsTopoOrder G l → ∀ (a b : V), G.Adj a b → List.idxOf a l < List.idxOf b l
theorems.doc: Every edge points forward.

theorems.name: BioMech.IsTopoOrder.acyclic
theorems.statement: ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq V] {G : Digraph V} {l : List V}, IsTopoOrder G l → Acyclic G
theorems.doc:
A digraph with a topological order is acyclic: positions in the order form
a rank.

theorems.name: BioMech.Pipeline.Stage.mem_all
theorems.statement: ∀ (s : Stage), s ∈ Stage.all
theorems.doc: `Stage.all` lists every stage.

theorems.name: BioMech.Pipeline.Stage.nodup_all
theorems.statement: Stage.all.Nodup
theorems.doc: `Stage.all` lists each stage once.

theorems.name: BioMech.Pipeline.Artefact.mem_all
theorems.statement: ∀ (a : Artefact), a ∈ Artefact.all
theorems.doc: `Artefact.all` lists every artefact.

theorems.name: BioMech.Pipeline.Artefact.nodup_all
theorems.statement: Artefact.all.Nodup
theorems.doc: `Artefact.all` lists each artefact once.

theorems.name: BioMech.Pipeline.Artefact.nodup_paths
theorems.statement: (List.map Artefact.path Artefact.all).Nodup
theorems.doc: Distinct artefacts have distinct paths.

theorems.name: BioMech.Pipeline.topoOrder_eq
theorems.statement:
topoOrder =
  [Stage.buildModel, Stage.loadModel, Stage.runStaticOpt, Stage.computeMomentArms,
    Stage.segmentPhases, Stage.labelRoles, Stage.enrichAnatomy, Stage.exportGraph,
    Stage.exportMeshes, Stage.exportMusclePaths, Stage.exportDynamics]
theorems.doc: The computed order, spelled out.

theorems.name: BioMech.Pipeline.isTopoOrder_topoOrder
theorems.statement: IsTopoOrder graph topoOrder
theorems.doc: `topoOrder` lists every stage once, each after all its predecessors.

theorems.name: BioMech.Pipeline.acyclic
theorems.statement: Acyclic graph
theorems.doc: The stage graph is acyclic.

theorems.name: BioMech.Pipeline.inputs_available
theorems.statement:
∀ (s : Stage),
  ∀ a ∈ s.reads, a.isSource = true ∨ ∃ p, a ∈ p.writes ∧ Relation.TransGen graph.Adj p s
theorems.doc: Every input of a stage is a source or the output of a stage upstream of it.

theorems.name: BioMech.Pipeline.writes_derived
theorems.statement: ∀ (s : Stage), ∀ a ∈ s.writes, a.isSource = false
theorems.doc:
Stages write derived files only: every output lands in `data/work/` or
`data/out/`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Pipeline.writer_unique
theorems.statement: ∀ (a : Artefact) (p q : Stage), a ∈ p.writes → a ∈ q.writes → p = q
theorems.doc: Each file has at most one writer.

theorems.name: BioMech.Pipeline.derived_written
theorems.statement: ∀ (a : Artefact), a.isSource = false → ∃ s, a ∈ s.writes
theorems.doc: Each derived file has a writer.

theorems.name: BioMech.Pipeline.read_unless_out
theorems.statement: ∀ (a : Artefact), a.dir ≠ Dir.out → ∃ s, a ∈ s.reads
theorems.doc:
Each source and each intermediate file feeds some stage; only the files in
`data/out/` leave the pipeline.

theorems.name: BioMech.Pipeline.buildModel_upstream
theorems.statement: ∀ (s : Stage), s ≠ Stage.buildModel → Relation.TransGen graph.Adj Stage.buildModel s
theorems.doc: `buildModel` runs upstream of every other stage.

theorems.name: BioMech.Pipeline.buildModel_sole_reader_of_scaled
theorems.statement: ∀ (s : Stage), Artefact.scaledModel ∈ s.reads ∨ Artefact.ikMotion ∈ s.reads ↔ s = Stage.buildModel
theorems.doc:
`buildModel` is the one stage that reads the scaled model or the
inverse-kinematics motion; every other stage loads the merged model and the
joint angles that carry the neck angles (D-008, D-010).

theorems.name: BioMech.Components.Component.mem_all
theorems.statement: ∀ (c : Component), c ∈ Component.all
theorems.doc: `Component.all` lists every component.

theorems.name: BioMech.Components.Component.nodup_all
theorems.statement: Component.all.Nodup
theorems.doc: `Component.all` lists each component once.

theorems.name: BioMech.Components.Component.nodup_paths
theorems.statement: (List.flatMap Component.paths Component.all).Nodup
theorems.doc: Each path belongs to exactly one component.

theorems.name: BioMech.Components.isTopoOrder_topoOrder
theorems.statement: IsTopoOrder graph topoOrder
theorems.doc:
`topoOrder` lists every component once, each importer before the modules
it imports.

theorems.name: BioMech.Components.acyclic
theorems.statement: Acyclic graph
theorems.doc: The import graph is acyclic, decided through reachability.

theorems.name: BioMech.Components.viewer3D_via_queryEngine
theorems.statement: ReachesOnlyVia graph Component.Viewer3D Component.QueryEngine Component.GraphStore
theorems.doc: `Viewer3D` reaches `GraphStore`, and only through `QueryEngine`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Components.phasePanel_via_queryEngine
theorems.statement: ReachesOnlyVia graph Component.PhasePanel Component.QueryEngine Component.GraphStore
theorems.doc: `PhasePanel` reaches `GraphStore`, and only through `QueryEngine`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Components.graphView_via_queryEngine
theorems.statement: ReachesOnlyVia graph Component.GraphView Component.QueryEngine Component.GraphStore
theorems.doc: `GraphView` reaches `GraphStore`, and only through `QueryEngine`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Components.timeline_via_queryEngine
theorems.statement: ReachesOnlyVia graph Component.Timeline Component.QueryEngine Component.GraphStore
theorems.doc: `Timeline` reaches `GraphStore`, and only through `QueryEngine`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Components.graphStore_behind_queryEngine
theorems.statement:
∀ (c : Component),
  c ≠ Component.App →
    c ≠ Component.QueryEngine →
      ¬Relation.TransGen (deleteVertex graph Component.QueryEngine).Adj c Component.GraphStore
theorems.doc:
The general rule behind the four theorems above: once `QueryEngine` is
deleted, `App` is the one component that still reaches `GraphStore`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Components.graphStore_importers
theorems.statement: ∀ (c : Component), graph.Adj c Component.GraphStore ↔ c = Component.QueryEngine ∨ c = Component.App
theorems.doc: `QueryEngine` and `App` are the two direct importers of `GraphStore`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Components.architectureView_reach
theorems.statement:
∀ (c : Component),
  Relation.TransGen graph.Adj Component.ArchitectureView c ↔ c = Component.TraceRecorder
theorems.doc:
`ArchitectureView` reaches exactly `TraceRecorder`: it stays clear of the
store and the query layer.

theorems.name: BioMech.Components.ui_imports_traceRecorder
theorems.statement: ∀ c ∈ ui, graph.Adj c Component.TraceRecorder
theorems.doc: Every UI component may import `TraceRecorder`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Components.leaves
theorems.statement: ∀ (c : Component), ¬graph.Adj Component.GraphStore c ∧ ¬graph.Adj Component.TraceRecorder c
theorems.doc:
`GraphStore` and `TraceRecorder` are leaves: their imports stay within
`sharedImports`.

theorems.name: BioMech.Components.app_root
theorems.statement:
∀ (c : Component),
  c ≠ Component.App →
    Relation.TransGen graph.Adj Component.App c ∧ ¬Relation.TransGen graph.Adj c Component.App
theorems.doc:
`App` is the root: it reaches every other component, and every other
component stays clear of it.
